intervals.label: Phase-I construction
intervals.note: Anchored to the Phase-I TDR (2018-12), the earliest dated evidence of the Phase-I programme found this session, as an approximate lower bound -- not a stated 'construction began' date. The collaboration's most recent dated activity found (collaboration meeting CM48, 27-31 July 2026) shows the programme is still ongoing; no data-taking or commissioning-complete statement was found.
intervals.quote: The Technical Design for the COMET Phase-I experiment is presented in this paper.

name: COMET detector
notes: technology_classes uses 'other': no listed technology_class names a curved-solenoid muon-transport spectrometer of this kind.

beam_power.quote: the 3.2 kW 8 GeV proton beam from J-PARC will be used.

summary.plain: A curved tunnel of superconducting magnets at the J-PARC laboratory in Japan that bends and slows down muons, feeding them into a detector built to catch the single electron that would appear if a muon converted into one.
summary.technical: Curved-solenoid pion capture and muon transport system selecting low-momentum, negatively-charged muons off an 8 GeV, 3.2 kW J-PARC proton beam, feeding a detector solenoid instrumented for Phase-I with CyDet (cylindrical drift chamber + trigger hodoscope) and, for background studies toward Phase-II, StrECAL (straw tracker + electromagnetic calorimeter).

technology.quote: Two types of detectors, CyDet and StrECAL, will be used for detecting the mu-e conversion events, and for measuring the beam-related background events in view of the Phase-II experiment, respectively.
technology.value: Curved superconducting solenoid pion/muon transport (capture and transport solenoids) feeding a detector solenoid instrumented with cylindrical drift chamber and trigger hodoscope (CyDet, Phase-I) or straw tracker and electromagnetic calorimeter (StrECAL)
